channel.title: HSJ - Latest news
channel.description: Custom RSS feed for HSJ latest news

item.title: Exclusive: ‘Landmark’ safety policy was barely tested before launch
item.description: The “Martha’s Rule for maternity services” was used just 13 times in a national pilot before being cited by government and adopted by ministers as a solution to the maternity crisis, HSJ can reveal.

item.title: Single water contract to save NHS £5m a year
item.description: NHS England is centralising the NHS’s water contracts in a move it says could save at least £5m a year.

item.title: Major trust freed after nine years of NHSE intervention
item.description: One of England’s largest hospital trusts has been freed from NHS England enforcement action that ran for almost a decade.

item.title: UK’s largest private hospital group sold in £1bn deal
item.description: One of the NHS’s largest private providers, Spire Healthcare Group, has agreed to a £1bn takeover by a group of investment firms.

item.title: Exclusive: Hundreds sacked for snooping on patient records
item.description: More than 200 NHS staff have been sacked and around 2,000 others sanctioned for inappropriately viewing patient records over the past five years, HSJ can reveal.

item.title: ICB plan says trust must cut staff by 15%
item.description: An acute trust would have to cut its workforce by almost 15 per cent and its costs by 26 per cent under a draft five-year plan set by its integrated care board.

item.title: Hot summer hit trust’s finances
item.description: An ambulance service will have to make an additional £1.6m in savings due to high demand over the hot summer and has been put under intense monitoring by NHS England.

item.title: Revealed: NHSE top team clear-out cost more than £800k
item.description: NHS England spent more than £800,000 on payouts for six directors last year as it cleared out its top team, it has been revealed.

item.title: ‘Process error’ leaves major supplier off £140m framework
item.description: A global market-leading medical device manufacturer has failed to join a key national framework worth up to £140m over four years – potentially disrupting supply and increasing costs to hospitals.

item.title: NHSE staff could be kept out of DHSC
item.description: Ministers and officials are considering whether to keep some NHS England functions and staff separate from the Department of Health and Social Care when the organisation is abolished next year, HSJ has learned.

item.title: NHS ends 12 years of staffing growth
item.description: The number of NHS staff in England is in year-on-year decline for the first time since 2013, as cuts to support and back-office roles combine with a sharp slowdown in clinical recruitment.

item.title: FDP is ‘here for the long term’, says NHSE boss
item.description: NHS England has vowed to press ahead with the controversial federated data platform and has insisted it is “here for the long term”, despite mounting pressure to cancel its contract with Palantir.

item.title: Many maternity units have ‘structural difficulties’, PM admits
item.description: The prime minister has admitted “structural difficulties” similar to those faced by a rural maternity unit recently forced to close over staff shortages are widespread across the NHS.

item.title: Recognise negative impact mutual aid can have on performance, pleads trust CEO
item.description: The chief executive of a trust that has fallen 34 places in NHS England’s provider performance league table has complained that the ranking fails to take into account its efforts to help neighbours.

item.title: Second trust’s delay telling Southport victims of data breaches was ‘appalling’
item.description: An ambulance trust waited nearly two months before informing victims of the 2024 Southport attack that their patient records may have been accessed inappropriately by staff, HSJ has discovered.

item.title: Government U-turns on ICB board change
item.description: The government has U-turned on Health Bill proposals to remove mandated council representation from integrated care boards.

item.title: Leading joint health and care deal falls foul of financial pressures
item.description: NHS financial pressures and reforms have brought about the end of one of the largest local joint health and social care funding arrangements.

item.title: How serial fraudster secured nine senior managerial roles
item.description: A fraudster secured 13 management and administrative jobs over 10 years, despite extensive pre- and post-recruitment checks by trusts, commissioners, national bodies, and recruitment agencies, HSJ has discovered.

item.title: Trust fails in bid to overturn CQC warning notice
item.description: One of the NHS’s most troubled trusts made an unsuccessful attempt to prevent the Care Quality Commission issuing it with a warning notice.

item.title: ICB bids to save its Healthwatch branch from abolition
item.description: An integrated care board is planning to pay £1.6m to retain its local Healthwatch for the next four years.
